correctness.rationale: For each m=3,4,5,6 the bidirected graph has 4m+2 arcs; valid faces have indegree/outdegree<=1 and no directed cycles. The complete exact finite complexes were independently enumerated, with all nonempty Hasse covers and deterministic acyclic Morse matchings verified, and signed integer Morse differentials recomputed by unit-pivot gradient cancellations. Critical cells: m3 one 0-, one 1-, eight 2-cells; m4 one 0-, eighteen 2-, one 3-cell; m5 one 0-, twenty-three 2-, thirty-two 3-cells; m6 one 0-, thirty-eight 2-, 169 3-cells. The nonzero integer boundary matrices at m3,m4,m5 have Smith invariant 2 (rank one; m5 nonzero coefficients share one target); m6 all vanish. For m3 the 1-skeleton is S1 and a degree-two 2-cell yields RP2 plus 7 S2; for m4,m5 Hurewicz pi2 of wedge S2 identifies degree-two Moore attachment and the remaining spheres; m6 all 3-cell attachments are null via pi2. This is exhaustive for exactly four finite objects, not an assertion for m>6.
residual_risks: Finite classification is exhaustive for four m values only. The derivation from the integer CW differentials to homotopy depends on low-dimensional attaching-map classification, not just homology ranks.

value.rationale: Triangular books form a natural increasing family of graph overlaps that adds a central edge to the better-studied bidirected K_{2,m} multipath examples. The exact integral transition from degree-one RP2 torsion at m3 through degree-two Moore summands at m4,m5 to a torsion-free wedge at m6 is a motivated non-monotone finite phenomenon, and the complete homotopy types (not merely Betti ranks) are useful standalone exact data. No extrapolation to m>6 is claimed; finite size is not inherently worthless.
residual_risks: The phenomenon at m6 does not prove a uniform large-m torsion-freeness theorem.

limitations: Entire claim covers precisely four fixed m, not arbitrary m; B3 is prior and not a discovery.
Signed acyclic integer Morse reductions are exhaustive for these four finite complexes only.
